title: Create a project in your tracker
summary: Create a project with its initial tasks in the team’s tracker.

parts.title: Draft the project brief and task breakdown
parts.guidance: Describe the result the project should produce, who needs it, the scope boundaries, and how the team will judge completion. Break it into tasks that each produce something reviewable, such as a design or a working import. Identify real dependencies and unresolved decisions. Link the source request and any existing work so the project brief gives the team a common starting point.

execution.rationale: The authored work for “Draft the project brief and task breakdown” is preparation, analysis or editing of supplied records with text, file or code tools. Any named human decisions and subsequent external actions retain their existing gates.

parts.title: Create the project and tasks in the tracker
parts.guidance: Search the intended team workspace for an existing project or overlapping tasks. Create the project from the brief, then add task descriptions, acceptance criteria, source links, and the dependencies already identified. Set visibility to match the material it contains. Check that every task belongs to the right project and return the project link with a short list of anything still missing, such as access to a supporting document.

execution.rationale: The supported path for “Create the project and tasks in the tracker” is a person working through the stated digital records, service or communication channel. Retain the named owners, approvals and expert review. This classification does not claim a verified agent integration or imply that future automation is impossible.

parts.title: Assign owners and due dates
parts.guidance: Agree an accountable owner for each task with the team doing the work. Work backward from real milestones, allowing for dependencies and capacity, and distinguish a committed due date from a tentative estimate. Update assignments and dates in the tracker, then flag unowned work or a dependency that makes the schedule impossible. The resulting plan should show who acts next and where a decision is needed to keep the project moving.

execution.rationale: The supported path for “Assign owners and due dates” is a person working through the stated digital records, service or communication channel. Retain the named owners, approvals and expert review. This classification does not claim a verified agent integration or imply that future automation is impossible.

metadata.supportReason: Project and task creation are core tracker APIs — a one-call agent step.
